historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are not usable growth proxies for BLK over this window: FY2025 diluted GAAP EPS fell 15.6% YoY (driven by the one-off acquisition/impairment/contingent-consideration charges and a step-up in the diluted share count from Subco unit issuance for the HPS deal, not operating deterioration), while reported FCF and owner FCF both compress the same year for the same reason. Shareholders' equity CAGR (14.0%) is elevated by the HPS all-equity acquisition currency (BLK issued ~$12.8B of stock/Subco units for HPS in July 2025), so it overstates organic compounding. Revenue CAGR (10.65% over 3yr, but 18.67% in the latest year alone, boosted by AUM step-ups from GIP/Preqin/HPS consolidation) is used as the primary anchor for the growth path, moderated down in the scenario build below because a meaningful share of FY2025's revenue growth is inorganic (M&A) rather than organic AUM/fee growth, which management itself reports separately at ~10%.

scenario_narratives.base: Acquisition-related noise (intangible amortization, contingent-consideration marks, one-off retention SBC) fades over 2-3 years; EBITDA margin recovers from FY2025's depressed 34% print back toward the FY2022-24 range and on to ~40-42% at maturity as technology (Aladdin) and private-markets revenue keep growing faster than the commoditized index/ETF base. Revenue growth decelerates from 10% (still partly HPS-annualization-driven) to a 4% terminal rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: GIP/Preqin/HPS integration is a clean success, private-credit and Aladdin both keep compounding at double-digit-plus rates, retirement-channel adoption (LifePath/Great Gray) opens new AUM faster than expected, and the '46% margin, not a ceiling' framing holds at the full-year level.
scenario_narratives.bear: A sustained capital-markets downturn compresses AUM/fees mechanically; index/ETF fee compression continues; the three-deal integration proves harder than guided with talent attrition and further impairments; political/regulatory (ESG divestment, SIFI risk) headwinds persist; margin stalls in the low-to-mid 30s rather than recovering.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BlackRock is valued as an operating company on owner free cash flow, not with a bank/REIT-style capitalization model: fee revenue on AUM is ordinary operating revenue, BlackRock's balance sheet carries real corporate debt (fixed-rate long-term notes) rather than customer deposits, and reported operating cash flow is a genuine (if presently noisy) measure of cash generation rather than a post-interest distributable-profit figure. The central judgment is that FY2025's reported margins and FCF are a trough distorted by the near-simultaneous GIP/Preqin/HPS acquisitions (intangible amortization, a large contingent-consideration fair-value charge, restructuring, and one-off retention stock compensation), not a new normal -- management's own as-adjusted operating margin was flat at ~39.6-39.7% through the acquisition window, which anchors the margin-recovery path used in the base case. A 10-year horizon is used because the FY2025 owner-FCF margin (7.9%) is far below any plausible steady state and needs the full period to mature.
key_risks_to_valuation: AUM/revenue is directly exposed to capital markets levels; a sustained bear market compresses base fees, performance fees, and margin simultaneously, independent of net flows

The margin-recovery assumption is the single largest driver of the base case -- if the GIP/Preqin/HPS integration keeps generating charges (further impairments, extended retention grants, contingent-consideration marks) rather than rolling off over 2-3 years as assumed, FY2025's depressed print could prove closer to the new normal than a trough
Fee compression in the commoditized index/ETF core is a structural headwind requiring continued AUM growth just to hold revenue flat in BlackRock's largest product category

Political/regulatory risk (state pension ESG divestments, periodic SIFI-designation discussion) is real but difficult to quantify and is not separately modelled beyond the bear-case margin/growth path

The Subco Class B-2 units (HPS deal consideration) are included in the fully diluted share count; if additional acquisition currency is issued this way in the future, the flat-share-count convention would need revisiting for genuine non-SBC dilution

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range $917.39-$1,219.94
data_sources.financials: research/BLK/Reports/BLK_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL-derived, FY2022-FY2025 annuals + quarterlies through Q2 2026); BlackRock, Inc. FY2025 10-K (CIK 0002012383, accession 0001193125-26-071966, filed 2026-02-25) for SBC detail (Note 18), employee tax withholdings and buyback cash flow (MD&A liquidity section and consolidated statements of cash flows/stockholders' equity), long-term borrowings (Note 15), diluted share reconciliation (Note 26), and the as-adjusted operating margin reconciliation (Executive Summary)

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 (filed 2026-02-25, accession 0001193125-26-071966): Note 18 Stock-Based Compensation, total SBC expense $1,307M (RSUs $1,282M incl. $394M one-off HPS/GIP incentive-retention awards, options $25M); MD&A liquidity discussion states $326M of employee tax withholdings related to employee stock transactions for 2025 (financing activities, distinct from the $1,951M 'Shares/Subco Units repurchased' cash-flow line). Combined SBC-incl-equity-taxes = 1,307 + 326 = 1,633. No single combined figure is published, so both lines are summed per the method's fallback rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0% built from a ~4.1% 10Y UST risk-free rate plus a ~5.5% US equity risk premium scaled by BLK's moderate-beta profile (asset manager with high operating leverage to markets but a diversified, recurring-fee, technology-subscription revenue base that dampens beta relative to a pure capital-markets business); no leverage adjustment needed given BLK's net debt is small (~$1.3B) relative to its ~$170B market cap.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- BlackRock's office leases are small relative to a $24B revenue, high-margin fee business; no separate lease line modelled (implicitly inside opex/EBITDA margin).
inputs.nci_treatment: Owner FCF is built off consolidated operating income and revenue, which include NCI - CIPs (consolidated investment products) and NCI - Subco (BlackRock Saturn Subco, the HPS all-equity-deal vehicle). Net income attributable to BlackRock, Inc. common shareholders is materially lower than consolidated net income once these are deducted, but the CIPs/Subco consolidation nets to roughly zero economic effect on a per-share basis because (a) CIP NCI represents non-recourse fund-level entities BlackRock does not own, largely self-funding and immaterial to enterprise FCF, and (b) Subco NCI (the ~7.6M Class B-2 units issued as HPS deal consideration) is captured by including the Subco units in the fully diluted share count used as the divisor. No separate NCI deduction is applied to the FCF bridge; the Subco dilution is handled entirely through the 163.156M fully diluted share count.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md routing table: BlackRock is an operating asset manager, not a bank/REIT/LIC -- fee revenue on AUM is ordinary operating revenue, free cash flow and net debt are both real and meaningful, so the standard owner-FCF engine applies, not a bank's residual-income-on-book approach). First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry exists. Net debt is small and POSITIVE ($1.3B: $12,768M fixed-rate long-term notes vs $11,468M cash) -- BlackRock is a net borrower, not a net-cash company, so interest income ($554M FY2025, mostly earned on seed/co-investment capital and regulatory/CIP-related balances, not a surplus cash pile) is NOT stripped from FCF; stripping it would be wrong here because there is no offsetting net-cash add-back to double-count against. FY2025 reported FCF and margins are depressed by one-off items tied to the near-simultaneous GIP/Preqin/HPS acquisitions: a $775M intangible amortization/impairment charge (up from $291M in FY2024), a $720M change-in-fair-value-of-contingent-consideration charge, a $39M restructuring charge, and $394M of one-off HPS/GIP incentive-retention SBC -- none of which are expected to recur at FY2025's scale. As-adjusted (management's own non-GAAP) operating margin was actually flat at ~39.6-39.7% in both FY2024 and FY2025, which is the basis for the margin-recovery path in the scenarios below rather than extrapolating the depressed GAAP print. A 10-year horizon is used because the FY2025 owner-FCF margin (7.9%) is nowhere near a mature/normalized level and needs the full horizon to ramp back through the historical FY2022-24 range (15.8-20.8%) and beyond as private-markets/technology mix shift plays out. D&A is built on the full cash-flow-statement depreciation-and-amortization figure ($1,126M FY2025, i.e. 4.65% of revenue), NOT the $297M PP&E-only figure embedded in the CSV's EBITDA column (EBITDA_csv = OperatingIncome + 297, which omits the $775M/829M of acquisition-related intangible amortization actually running through operating expense) -- using the narrower figure would understate the real non-cash add-back and materially misstate NOPAT.

bear.narrative: Bear case: a sustained equity/bond bear market mechanically compresses AUM, base fees and performance fees simultaneously (BlackRock's own top-listed business risk), while fee compression in the commoditized index/ETF core continues to bite. The GIP/Preqin/HPS integration proves harder than guided -- private-credit fundraising slows as the credit cycle turns, key private-markets investment talent attrition follows the ~18-month, three-deal integration window, and goodwill/intangible impairments recur (as already seen once in FY2024 and again via the FY2025 contingent-consideration mark). Political/ESG-driven state pension divestments and SIFI-designation regulatory risk add a persistent AUM and multiple headwind. EBITDA margin stalls in the low-to-mid 30s rather than recovering to the pre-acquisition ~40% level, SBC stays structurally elevated as retention grants are extended to keep private-markets talent, and the cash tax rate ramps up modestly on reduced use of favorable entity-structure benefits.

base.narrative: Base case: BlackRock's FY2025 acquisition-related charges (intangible amortization, contingent-consideration mark, restructuring, one-off retention SBC) roll off over the next 2-3 years as GIP/Preqin/HPS integration completes, and EBITDA margin recovers from the depressed 34% FY2025 print back through the FY2022-24 range (36.6-38.4%) and on to ~40-42% at maturity as the higher-margin technology (Aladdin) and private-markets/performance-fee revenue mix continues to grow faster than the commoditized index/ETF base, consistent with management's stated target of technology + private markets exceeding 30% of revenue by 2030. Revenue growth decelerates from 10% (still capturing some annualization of HPS base fees plus continued ~9-10% organic net-inflow-driven growth) toward a 4% terminal rate reflecting a mature, still-compounding but no-longer-hypergrowth global AUM franchise. SBC-as-%-of-revenue declines from an elevated 6.5% (inflated by one-off HPS/GIP retention grants) toward a steady-state ~4.5%. D&A stays elevated near-term from acquired-intangible amortization before declining as those intangibles run off. Working-capital capture is held at zero: as a fee-based asset manager, BlackRock carries essentially no inventory or trade receivables/payables cycle tied to revenue growth (client cash and CIP balances are balance-sheet pass-throughs, not owner-FCF working capital).

bull.narrative: Bull case: the GIP/Preqin/HPS integration is a clean success -- private-credit AUM (targeted by BlackRock and management to more than double to $4.5T market-wide by 2030) and Aladdin/technology ACV both compound at their recent double-digit-plus rates, retirement-channel private-markets adoption (LifePath/Great Gray) opens a large new AUM pool faster than expected, and record net inflows ($868B TTM) continue near current pace rather than reverting toward the industry mean. Management's '46% is not a ceiling' framing proves out at the full-year level (not just one strong quarter), technology + private markets exceed the 30%-of-revenue-by-2030 target ahead of schedule, and continued strong capital markets support AUM levels. Buybacks continue at or above the raised $550M/quarter guidance, funded by the resulting stronger FCF.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default (15/50/35) shifted 5pp from bull to bear. BLK carries no going-concern or solvency risk (net debt is trivial relative to a ~$170B market cap and cash flow is strongly positive throughout even the bear case), which argues against raising bear weight on balance-sheet grounds -- but the bull case here needs several distinct things to go right simultaneously (private-credit market growth at the pace BlackRock itself projects, successful integration of three near-simultaneous acquisitions, continued record net inflows persisting rather than reverting toward the industry's longer-run mean, and margin expansion beyond the already-elevated levels management is guiding to), while the bear case is a single, well-precedented axis (a capital-markets drawdown mechanically hits AUM-based revenue, which is BlackRock's own top-listed risk factor) with real historical precedent (2022's bond/equity bear market). The extra weight comes from bull, not from inventing new bear risk.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
